reason: Confirmed by driving chromium at ?v=light&motion=settled and measuring every line box with a per-character Range walk, not by eye. Source checks out: lately.html:433 `.limits { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) }`, lately.html:557 collapses it to `1fr` inside `@media (max-width: 900px)`, and `.limit .t-small` (lately.html:901) has computed max-width: none at every width. Measured line-one character counts for the three refusal bodies: 1440 and 1280 -> 49/53/55; 901 -> 34/32/37; 900 -> 115/121/119; 899 -> 115/118/119; 793 -> 94/100/104; 768 (a committed frame, shots/light-full--768x1024.png) -> 94/95/98; 561 -> 60/63/64. So the one-pixel swing is real and is 3.2x on the worst paragraph (119 at 900 against 37 at 901), and the whole 561-900 band is set beyond any measure a studio at this bar ships. It reproduces identically in full, partial, quiet and first-run, i.e. in every state that renders the protected movement. The `.note .t-body` half also checks out arithmetically -- 62ch at 15px computes to 616.59px because ch is the zero glyph (9.95px) and not a character, and the note sets 91 characters on line one -- with one correction that runs in the finding's favour and against its framing: that note is capped at 616.59px at 1440 and 1280 too, so it sets 91 characters at the reference width, not only in the tablet band. Two of the seat's stated numbers are off by a word range: 121 at 900 and 118 at 899 belong to the SECOND refusal, not the third (the third is 119 at both), and 768 measures 98 not 97. Neither moves the argument. This is also the paid-for class in lessons.md creeping back from the other side -- 'The measure has a floor AND a ceiling' -- and neither gate can see it: audit.mjs scores palette, weight, contrast, targets, radii, motion, ramp and leading, and interaction-check.mjs asserts only that the movement is present with three tiles at the same rank (lines 404-421, 1270). Nothing in 461 assertions reads a line length. Severity holds at defect: nothing is asserted untrue and the product still does what it says, but a 121-character line of 13px type is visibly wrong in the one movement whose job is to be believed. The seat's fix is confirmed only in its load-bearing third; the other two thirds are corrected in sharpenedFix.
sharpenedFix: Keep the ceiling, drop the other two rules, and set the number from what paints rather than from ch -- which is the finding's own argument, applied to its own fix. (1) `.limit .t-small { max-width: 330px; }`. Driven, 330px yields 49/58 - 53/54 - 55/54 across the band and is inert at 1440 (column content box 318.7px) and at 390 (310px), so it bites only where the grid has collapsed and it lands the band on the same 49-55 measure the three-column layout already delivers -- which is what the seat promised and what its own 42ch does not deliver: 42ch computes to 361.998px and yields up to 64 characters on line one, about 16% wider than the measure it claims to match. (2) DROP `.limit .t-head { max-width: 40ch }` entirely. 40ch at 20px computes to 546.4px; the three heads are 16-20 characters and render at 171/193/180px, so this rule can never bite at any width from 390 to 1440. It is inert CSS shipped into a stylesheet this lab has already had a finding filed against for dead rules. (3) LEAVE `.note .t-body { max-width: 62ch }` out of this change, or take it as its own decision with its own frames. Its 91-character line is real but it is not a tablet-band defect -- it is identical at 1440 and 1280 -- so folding it in here smuggles a change to the partial state at the reference width in under a band-scoped rationale. And 46ch computes to 457.47px and yields 66/69, not the 48-54 the finding names as the design's intent; if it is taken at all the honest number is ~300px (the note is a flex row, so a narrower body also changes how much of the panel the paragraph fills, which is a composition call, not a measure call). Also worth folding in while the movement is open, since the seat missed it in the same band: `.ghost-say .t-small` (lately.html:908) has no ceiling either and sets its 79-character sentence on one unbroken line at 466px at EVERY width including 1440, immediately below the three refusals it is meant to sit with -- `.ghost-say .t-head` is capped at 34ch and its sibling body is not.
breaks: Small blast radius, but not zero. (1) Frames: the refusal movement re-flows in the 561-900 band, so shots/light-full--768x1024.png must be re-shot, and .limit is a flex column with gap so the tiles grow a line each (2 lines -> 3 at 900, 2 -> 3 at 768); re-measure total page height and anything downstream that assumes it. The 1440, 1280 and 390 frames are untouched by the 330px cap -- verify that by measuring the .t-small box (must stay 318.7px at 1440/1280 and 310px at 390), not by diffing pixels. (2) The refusal tiles are `.limit rise` with --i:1; the entrance is unchanged but the taller tile means re-running the settled-frame reproducibility check, since the round-2 note records twenty-six of fifty-six frames differing between runs on entrance timing. (3) The paragraph now stops short of its own tile's right edge in the band, leaving ~190px of --paper-3 to its right at 900; that is the intended trade but it is a visible composition change in a protected movement, so it wants a founder look at 768 before it is called finished. (4) Re-run both gates: audit.mjs at every configured viewport (the type-ramp and leading checks read computed style on these nodes) and interaction-check.mjs, whose limits block at lines 404-421 counts three tiles and compares the movement's heading rank -- neither should move, and if either does, the cap has hit something it should not. (5) If the .ghost-say .t-small addition is taken, that one DOES change 1440, so light-full--1440x960.png and its six sibling state frames need re-shooting.
